sm: Albert Mohler opens by describing a major espionage story. Reports said US agencies were focused on a woman called Alice Huang, suspected of being a Chinese spy, and it then emerged that the real center of the story was Jensen Huang, the president and CEO of Nvidia, who was reportedly in a romantic relationship with her. Mohler says the story is revealing in moral terms because it involves adultery as well as intellectual theft and national security. He frames the contest over high technology as one between the United States and communist China, and notes decades of Chinese espionage. He then begins on a Wall Street Journal timeline, starting with a company called Megaspede, created in 2023 as a spinoff of a Chinese firm.

Mohler continues the Wall Street Journal timeline. US agencies suspect China uses fronts in other Asian countries to buy restricted chips. The timeline includes photos of Jensen Huang with Alice Huang in Taipei in 2024 and 2025, a Commerce Department investigation of Megaspede, and a Trump decision in December 2025 to allow H-200 chip exports to China in exchange for 25 percent of sales. In spring 2026, Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised a classified memo warning about the relationship, and the Justice Department took over the investigation. Mohler says the story is dominating front pages, pushing aside the midterms and other news. He then reads the start of an apology letter Huang wrote to Nvidia colleagues.

Mohler reads the rest of Jensen Huang's letter, in which Huang says he was unfaithful to his wife, apologizes to his family and colleagues, and says Nvidia's board has started an independent investigation that he will cooperate with. Mohler says authorities care less about the adultery than about how much information or manipulation was involved. He cites a New York Times report that a Commerce Department chip inquiry was halted after Nvidia intervened, and says President Trump acknowledged a criminal investigation by the FBI and others. Speaking as a Christian, Mohler notes the Ten Commandments forbid adultery. He argues that Huang's shame shows people are made as moral creatures, and that the episode refutes the idea of sex without consequences.

Mohler says no one of public consequence is claiming the affair is no big deal. He notes the Huang family is reported to be worth at least 4.5 billion dollars, and says sin ultimately shows up as stupidity. He compares Huang to Samson and Delilah, saying the woman wanted what a powerful man had. Powerful men can control themselves, he says, but they choose not to. Turning to the midterm elections, he says Los Angeles, New York and Washington, D.C. will now have openly Democratic Socialist mayors, including Zohran Mamdani in New York. He also mentions a Democratic Senate win in Michigan, a Democratic governor in Texas, and James Talarico's Senate win. Mohler calls this a massive shift to the left.
